newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Two of Sweden's big banks explore merger - paper.
newsitem.headline: Two of Sweden's big banks explore merger - paper.

text.p: Two of Sweden's big four banks have started tentative merger talks, Sweden's business newspaper Dagens Industri said on Saturday.
The newspaper said representatives from S-E-Banken approached their counterparts at Handelsbanken to discuss the possibility.
The two banks are rivals in Sweden's competitive banking sector but Dagens Industri said the need for a strong position in Europe's Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) was the reason behind the talks.
"The two believe that it is better to merge than to be bought up by foreign banks," the paper said.
S-E-Banken, owned by Sweden's Wallenberg dynasty, would have the stronger influence in a merged bank as someone from that bank would probably be appointed chairman of the board.
Handelsbanken chief executive Arne Martensson would likely become chief executive officer of a merged bank.
The paper said the merger would be tough as both banks have extremely different corporate cultures.
It said if there was any decision to go ahead, it was expected to be made during the first half of next year at the latest.
The paper said a merger would cut costs by 25 percent and boost profits by 35 percent.
